sections.section_name: Section B - Very Short Spatial Interpretations

questions.question_text: Explain the physical mechanism and spatial parameters of chemical weathering known as 'hydration'. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Hydration occurs when rock minerals chemically absorb water and expand in volume. This structural modification creates internal strain, causing the rock framework to break down into grains over time.

questions.question_text: Define the concept of planetary 'albedo' and identify the surface type with the highest albedo value. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Albedo is the proportion of incoming solar radiation reflected back into space by Earth's surface. Fresh snow and ice surfaces possess the highest global albedo values, reflecting maximum energy.

questions.question_text: Explain the formation mechanism of a 'meander' in a mature river system. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Meanders form in floodplains where lateral erosion dominates. Water flows faster on the outer bend, eroding the bank, while slower water on the inner bend deposits accumulated fluvial sediments.

sections.section_name: Section C - Short Analytical & Comparative Studies

questions.question_text: Construct a comparative differentiation table outlining three distinct physical properties separating ocean waves from ocean currents. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Ocean waves represent the oscillatory movement of water particles where energy travels horizontally while water particles move in small circles. Ocean currents involve the actual, large-scale horizontal movement of water masses over immense geographic distances driven by dominant winds.

questions.question_text: Differentiate between absolute humidity and relative humidity within atmospheric climatology. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Absolute humidity measures the actual mass of water vapor present in a specific volume of air. Relative humidity is the percentage ratio of actual moisture present compared to the maximum moisture capacity of the air at that specific temperature.

questions.question_text: Identify and explain two primary forces that initiate and control the directional flow of global ocean currents. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The primary initiating force is surface wind friction, which drags surface water horizontally. The secondary controlling force is the Coriolis effect, which structurally deflects current trajectories to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and left in the Southern Hemisphere.

questions.question_text: Describe the thermal characteristics of the troposphere and explain the significance of the normal lapse rate. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The troposphere is the lowest atmospheric layer where all weather occurs. Its defining thermal characteristic is the normal lapse rate, where temperature decreases steadily by 6.5°C for every 1000 meters of increased altitude due to terrestrial radiation.

questions.question_text: Differentiate between the propagation dynamics of Primary (P) waves and Secondary (S) waves generated during an earthquake. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: P-waves are fast longitudinal waves that travel parallel to the propagation direction through solids, liquids, and gases. S-waves are slower transverse waves that vibrate perpendicular to propagation and can only travel through solid structural mediums, helping map the core.

questions.question_text: Outline two critical pieces of geological evidence Alfred Wegener utilized to support the Continental Drift Theory. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Wegener highlighted the jigsaw-puzzle fit of the South American and African coastlines. Furthermore, he presented the distribution of identical Mesosaurus fossils across these widely separated continents, proving they were once joined in the supercontinent Pangaea.

questions.question_text: Construct a brief differentiation outline separating the formation processes of igneous and sedimentary rocks. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Igneous rocks crystallize directly from cooling and solidifying magma or lava from the Earth's interior. Sedimentary rocks form through the gradual accumulation, compaction, and lithification of eroded mineral fragments or organic matter over extended geological timescales.

questions.question_text: Read the following case context: Meteorologists tracking a tropical weather cell notice a sharp pressure drop near the center loop, followed by rapid anticlockwise wind convergence in the Northern Hemisphere. Identify the weather framework, describe its core pressure gradient, and analyze the cloud layout. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: This weather layout is a cyclone. It features a deep low-pressure system at its center, which draws in high-velocity winds from surrounding boundaries. As moist air ascends quickly along the isobar walls, it condenses to form thick cumulonimbus clouds that bring torrential rain.

questions.question_text: Read the context: Seismologists map a global network of volcanic arcs and deep ocean trenches surrounding the Pacific Ocean basin, noting extreme tectonic activity. Identify this geographical feature, describe its boundary interaction type, and explain the resulting geological events. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: This feature is the Pacific Ring of Fire. It exists along convergent plate boundaries where dense oceanic plates undergo subduction beneath lighter continental plates. This intense friction and melting generate powerful earthquakes and continuous volcanic eruptions along the trench zones.

questions.question_text: Deconstruct the structural evolution of erosional landforms created entirely by the continuous physical actions of valley glaciers, detailing three distinct geometric shapes and integrating specific spatial coordinate labeling indices for Alpine glaciated regions (e.g., 46° N, 8° E). [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Glaciers erode alpine valleys (Map Index: 46° N, 8° E) through plucking and abrasion. They transform narrow V-shaped gorges into steep, flat-bottomed U-shaped troughs. Plucking carves out deep, armchair-like steep depressions called cirques. Where multiple cirque walls erode backward toward a central peak, they sharpen the rock into a jagged, pyramid-like landform known as a horn.

questions.question_text: Deconstruct the global model of atmospheric pressure belts and planetary wind systems, detailing the trade winds and westerlies. Include explicit spatial labeling indices for the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) map location. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Global circulation features distinct pressure belts driving planetary winds. Trade winds blow from subtropical highs toward the equator, converging at the ITCZ (Map Index: 5° N to 5° S), generating heavy precipitation. Westerlies flow from subtropical highs toward subpolar lows. The Coriolis effect dictates their structural deflection, mapping global climate zones precisely.
